title: Operator session audit proxy and KMS usage attributor
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds operator session audit proxy and server-side attribution of KMS calls; no public API changes.
description:
Summary: Introduce a lightweight operator-session-aware audit proxy and a KMS usage attributor that binds KMS requests to operator session assertions and RBAC v2 decisions. Motivation: customers and SRE teams requested stronger non-repudiable attribution for operator-driven KMS operations and clearer audit trails for cross-tenant/operator activity (see SEC-210). This PR provides a server-side shim that enriches audit records with operator_session_id, resolved RBAC decision trace, and a KMS call nonce that links the crypto operation to the audit record.

What changed (high-level):
- services/auditproxy: new service that accepts internal operator session-forwarded requests, validates operator JWTs, fetches RBAC v2 decisions via the policy-evaluator, attaches decision-trace metadata, and forwards requests to the KMS facade with an attributor nonce.
- pkg/kms/attributor.go: new package that generates deterministic per-request attribution tokens (HMACed nonce with key rotation support) and exposes Verify/Annotate helpers for downstream services.
- rbac/v2/policies/operator_bindings.yaml: RBAC v2 policy templates to ensure operators cannot escalate cross-region KMS usage; adds policy conditions for operator_session_id presence and region pin.
- api/docs/audit-proxy.md: operational runbook, rollout steps, config knobs (audit retention, signing key rotation, rate limits).
- tests/integration/auditproxy_e2e_test.go: end-to-end tests that simulate operator sessions and assert attribution propagation into audit logs and KMS call metadata.
- infra/helm/audit-proxy-values.yaml: optional helm chart values for Dedicated/Private deployments (feature gated by platform flag).

Commit summary:
- a1b2c3d Add initial auditproxy skeleton, JWT validation and proxying
- b2c3d4e Implement KMS attributor and deterministic nonce format
- c3d4e5f Wire RBAC v2 policy checks into proxy; add policy templates
- d4e5f6a Add e2e tests and fixture operator session tokens
- e5f6a7b Docs and helm values

Files changed (high-level): services/auditproxy/*, pkg/kms/attributor.go, rbac/v2/policies/operator_bindings.yaml, tests/integration/auditproxy_e2e_test.go, api/docs/audit-proxy.md, infra/helm/audit-proxy-values.yaml

Behavioral notes and invariants:
- The audit proxy does not change public REST surface for customers; it is an internal server-to-server shim used by operator tooling and RBAC enforcement. Deployments can opt-in by enabling the feature-flag `operator_session_audit_proxy`.
- KMS nonces are HMACed with a platform signing key and carry a bounded timestamp window (default 30s) to reduce replay risk. The attributor exposes verification endpoints for offline auditors.
- RBAC v2 policies introduced require operator_session_id to be present for any operator-scoped KMS role grants. Missing session IDs cause a deny decision and are logged for SRE investigation.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Marcus Liu (reviewer): "Nice isolation of attributor logic. Two asks: (1) show how keys rotate without breaking verification of recent nonces, (2) prefer context.Context threading rather than global logger in pkg/kms/attributor.go." — Addressed in commit d4e5f6a (added key-rotation grace window and context propagation).
- Diego Ramirez: "We should ensure the audit proxy masks tenant PII before forwarding; add a sanitizer step." — Implemented in b2c3d4e (sanitizer middleware) and added tests that assert PII redaction.
- Claire Morgan: "Operationally, we need metrics for attributed KMS calls per-operator and per-tenant; add Prometheus counters and dashboards." — Added counters in e5f6a7b and a Grafana template in api/docs.
- CIbot: flagged a flaky test on first run (tests/integration/auditproxy_e2e_test.go) — rerun passed. A slow e2e was quarantined and marked with [slow].

CI summary:
- unit (go test ./...): pass
- lint (golangci-lint): pass
- integration (sanity subset): pass
- e2e (slow): flaked once, rerun passed
- security-scan (deps): pass

Backwards compatibility and migration:
- No breaking public API changes. Existing operator tooling must set operator_session_id header when calling internal KMS endpoints to get attributed audit entries; fallback behavior logs an audit warning and denies RBAC policies created by this PR.
- Migration plan: staged rollout across regions: enable in Canary -> Dedicated staging -> global. Helm chart exposes `operatorSession.audit.enabled` and `kmsAttributor.rotationWindow`.

Rollout and monitoring
- Initial rollout gated behind feature flag and a 96-hour canary window. We will monitor:
  - audit.attributed_kms_calls_total by region/operator
  - audit.missing_session_id_denies_total
  - auditproxy.request_latency_ms P95
  - integration test healthcheck signals

Related work and references: SEC-210 (attribution requirements), ENG-9991 (policy-evaluator compatibility changes), design doc link: internal.redwood/docs/operator-session-audit-proxy (arch diagrams and threat model).

Reason for merge: All review comments addressed, CI green after rerun, E2E flake quarantined and tracked (ENG-10004). Merged via squash to preserve coherent change set and make rollback simpler. Post-merge actions: deploy helm chart to staging, coordinate with SRE to quarantine traffic if audit anomalies spike.
